questions.prompt: Name one observation that suggests dark matter exists.
questions.answer: Galaxy rotation curves, gravitational lensing, and galaxy-cluster motion all suggest more gravitating mass than visible matter can provide.

questions.prompt: What is dark energy associated with observationally?
questions.answer: Dark energy is associated with the observed accelerated expansion of the universe.

questions.prompt: Why are neutrino masses an open question for particle physics?
questions.answer: Neutrino oscillations show neutrinos have mass, but the origin and exact pattern of those masses are not fully explained by the simplest Standard Model.

questions.prompt: State the enclosed-mass estimate for circular orbital speed \(v\) at radius \(r\).
questions.answer:
\[
M(r)=\frac{v^2r}{G}
\]
This connects observed orbital speed to gravitating mass.

questions.prompt: Why does a flat galaxy rotation curve imply increasing enclosed mass?
questions.answer: If \(v\) stays roughly constant, then \(M(r)=v^2r/G\) increases with \(r\). More mass is inferred at larger radii than the visible matter suggests.

questions.prompt: What is meant by the matter-antimatter asymmetry?
questions.answer: The observable universe contains much more matter than antimatter, even though many particle laws treat matter and antimatter nearly symmetrically.

questions.prompt: Why is ordinary dim matter not enough to explain dark matter evidence?
questions.answer: Dark matter evidence affects galaxy dynamics, lensing, and cosmic structure in ways that exceed limits on ordinary baryonic matter from cosmology and nucleosynthesis.

questions.prompt: What does \(\Omega_\Lambda\) represent in cosmology notation?
questions.answer: \(\Omega_\Lambda\) represents the density fraction associated with dark energy or the cosmological-constant-like component.

questions.prompt: Explain why quantum gravity is an open problem.
questions.answer: The Standard Model is quantum, but gravity is described by general relativity as spacetime geometry. A tested theory combining quantum principles with gravity is not yet established.

questions.prompt: A star orbits at \(2.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at radius \(3.0\times10^{20}\,\mathrm m\). Estimate the enclosed mass.
Why must dark matter interact gravitationally?
questions.answer: Dark matter is inferred from gravitational effects: orbital speeds, lensing, and structure formation. Whatever it is, it must contribute to gravity.

questions.prompt: Why does dark matter not have to interact strongly with light?
questions.answer: It is dark because it does not emit, absorb, or scatter light strongly enough to be seen directly. Its main observed effect is gravitational.

questions.prompt: What would make a proposed dark-matter particle scientifically useful?
questions.answer: It should explain gravitational observations, fit cosmological constraints, make testable predictions, and be consistent with particle experiments and astrophysical data.

questions.prompt: Explain why accelerated expansion cannot be concluded from redshift alone.
questions.answer: Redshift shows expansion, but acceleration requires comparing distance, redshift, and cosmic history. Supernova and other data reveal that expansion has changed over time.

questions.prompt: Why are open questions not evidence that the Standard Model is useless?
questions.answer: The Standard Model remains extremely accurate within its tested domain. Open questions mark where additional theory is needed, not where existing successful predictions fail wholesale.

questions.prompt: A galaxy rotation curve remains flat out to large radius. Use \(M(r)=v^2r/G\) to describe the mass profile.
questions.answer: If \(v\) is constant, then \(M(r)\propto r\). The enclosed gravitating mass keeps increasing roughly linearly with radius, suggesting an extended dark-matter halo.

questions.prompt: Why do neutrino oscillations imply that neutrino flavour is not the same as fixed mass?
questions.answer: A neutrino produced with one flavour can later be detected as another. That requires flavour states to be mixtures of different mass states that evolve differently in time.

questions.prompt: Explain why matter-antimatter asymmetry is linked to early-universe physics.
questions.answer: Matter and antimatter would have annihilated in equal amounts if produced perfectly symmetrically. The present excess of matter must have arisen from early-universe processes that generated a small imbalance.

questions.prompt: Why is dark energy described as a cosmology problem rather than a laboratory particle discovery so far?
questions.answer: Its evidence comes mainly from the large-scale expansion history of the universe. No laboratory particle or field explanation has been confirmed as the source of dark energy.

questions.prompt: Give two criteria for judging a proposed solution beyond the Standard Model.
questions.answer: It should reproduce the Standard Model where it is already tested and explain at least one unresolved observation. It should also make predictions that can be checked by experiments or observations.
